tables.description: Description and summary statistics of the 20 industry portfolios (SIC codes, stock counts, market-cap share, excess returns, size/BE/ME-adjusted abnormal returns, F-tests).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct universe and industry construction: monthly formation of the 20 value-weighted industry portfolios from CRSP time-varying 2-digit SIC codes (July 1963-July 1995), NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ coverage, market-capitalization computation (|prc| x shrout), excess returns over the 3-month T-bill, and the Daniel-Titman 5x5 size/BE/ME characteristic-matched abnormal returns (January 1973-July 1995 subperiod). Stock counts and cap shares jointly pin down the SIC grouping definitions in Table I rows.
tables.paper_quote: The average number of stocks assigned to each industry portfolio every month is reported, along with the minimum number of stocks appearing in each portfolio at any point in time (reported in parentheses). Also reported are the average percentage of total market capitalization, the average return in excess of the three-month Treasury bill rate, the return standard deviation, and the average abnormal return in excess of size and BE/ME matched benchmarks ( $t$ -statistics are in parentheses) of each industry over the sample period (L127)

tables.description: Momentum profits for individual equities, industries, and random industries (6,6 strategy), Panels A-C.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of the (6,6) momentum strategies and the paper's central decomposition: 30%-breakpoint value-weighted individual stock momentum with overlapping-portfolio averaging, industry momentum (long top-3 / short bottom-3 of the 20 industries, equal-weighted across industries, VW within), the DGTW 125-portfolio characteristic adjustment, random-industry return replacement, and the industry-neutral, excess-industry, and high-industry-loser alternative portfolios.
tables.paper_quote: Panel B reports average monthly profits of momentum strategies of industries, where industries are sorted on their past six-month raw returns and a zero investment strategy is formed that is long the three highest past return industries and short the three lowest, holding the positions constant for six months, and recomputing the strategy monthly. (L368)

tables.description: Industry momentum trading profits IM(L,H) for L in {1,6,12}, H in {1,6,12,24,36}, with (Panel A) and without (Panel B) a skipped month; Wi, Lo, Wi-Lo, Wi-Mid, Mid-Lo, and DGTW rows.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates temporal robustness of industry momentum across the full IM(L,H) horizon grid with and without a skipped month, including the buy-side (Wi-Mid) vs sell-side (Mid-Lo) decomposition and DGTW-adjusted profits - validating the overlapping-hold / monthly-rebalance mechanics and the industry momentum ranking at every horizon.
tables.paper_quote: Ranking the 20 industries based on their $L$-month lagged returns, we form portfolios of the highest and lowest past performing industries, hold them for $H$ months, and rebalance monthly. Again, our strategy is long the highest three past performing industries and short the lowest three. (L704)
tables.notes: All 180 mean cells across Panels A-B are replicated; t-stat cells are included wherever the parsed paper preserves them (all rows at L=1; DGTW rows at L=6 and L=12) - the parse dropped the other t-stat rows of Table III, so those t-stats are not contracted.

tables.description: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions of size/BE/ME-adjusted returns on beta, log size, BE/ME, and individual (ret) and industry (ind) past-return variables across (6,1)/(6,6)/(12,1)/(12,12) horizons, Panels A-D (January 1973-July 1995).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regression methodology on Daniel-Titman characteristic-adjusted returns: pre-ranking beta smoothing (36-month rolling regression on the CRSP value-weighted index, 100 equal-weighted beta groups), log size and log BE/ME regressors, individual and industry past-return variables at four horizons, time-series averaged coefficients with FM t-stats, and the paper's key interaction result that 6-month industry momentum subsumes 6-month individual stock momentum (Panels C-D).
tables.paper_quote: Fama and MacBeth (1973) cross-sectional regressions are run every month on the universe of securities from January 1973–July 1995. (L1496)
